signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Monetary Divergence
signals.text: The G10 Currency Scorecard flags a major bilateral divergence: CHF 1W average performance sits at +1.051% across 6 pairs, while AUD is the clear G10 laggard at -1.718% across 4 pairs, creating a 2.770% leader-to-laggard spread. AUD/CHF trades at 0.5656, reflecting heavy selling pressure that pushes the pair well below its SMA20/50/200 cluster (SMA20 at 0.5697, SMA50 at 0.5753, SMA200 at 0.5760). RBA policy rate at 4.85% vs SNB at 0.00% yields a +485bp nominal carry advantage for AUD, but this yield support is currently failing to offset broad-based risk-off capital flows and safe-haven CHF demand. ESI data reinforces the fundamental split, with Switzerland scoring +35.9 (strong positive beats) while Australia sits neutral-to-negative at -4.6. Trend structure shows an explicit downtrend in force across AUD pairs, accelerating on wide-range bearish daily bars. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/CHF, strong G10 relative performance divergence overpowering carry. Catalyst: US Nonfarm Payrolls release at 13:30 UTC. Risk: Severe equity market rebound that triggers rapid unwinding of safe-haven CHF positions.

signals.title: GBP/USD — BoE Hawkish Repricing + Technical Cluster Test
signals.text: Bank of England Governor Bailey explicitly noted that inflation remains baked in due to energy price caps, coinciding with sell-side confirmation of a hawkish BoE rate hike to 4.25%. BoE at 4.25% (HIKING) vs Fed at 4.00% (ON HOLD) maintains a -25bp carry deficit for USD (SONIA 3.74% vs SOFR 3.97% gives a 23bp OIS carry advantage to USD). GBP/USD trades at 1.3449, holding firmly above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (SMA20 at 1.3342, SMA50 at 1.3366, SMA200 at 1.3423). CFTC positioning shows Leveraged Funds net long +20,016 contracts (long% 59.8%, 52-week percentile 37), showing positioning is not yet crowded despite recent gains. Retail sentiment data retail sentiment shows 65% short, establishing a contrarian institutional bias in favor of continued upside. Trade bias: Bullish GBP/USD, supported by central bank hawkishness and intact technical moving-average support. Catalyst: BoE MPC Member Pill Speech at 12:15 UTC. Risk: US NFP blowout at 13:30 UTC causing an aggressive hawkish repricing of Fed policy.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Support vs Options Downside Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 157.71, capped below its 20-day moving average of 157.95 but holding above the 50-day moving average at 157.33 within a tight 20-session box. A +275bp policy rate spread (Fed 4.00% vs BoJ 1.25%, with OIS SOFR 3.97% vs TONA 1.23% providing +274bp carry) continues to favor USD, but structural option flows diverge. 25-delta risk reversals exhibit a strong put skew of -1.80 (Saxo 1M tenor), indicating institutional demand for downside JPY protection even as net CFTC Leveraged Fund positioning remains short JPY at -19,224 contracts (long% 44.3%, pctl 94, z +1.57). 160.00 remains the critical level that has previously triggered verbal intervention warnings from Ministry of Finance officials. Trade bias: Range-bound USD/JPY, carry support offset by downside options hedging. Catalyst: US Nonfarm Payrolls at 13:30 UTC. Risk: Sustained close above 158.63 (200-day SMA) that forces option put unwind.

signals.title: NZD/USD — Retail Extreme vs ESI Data Headwind
signals.text: NZD/USD trades at 0.5595, bound beneath its entire moving average matrix (SMA20 at 0.5642, SMA50 at 0.5703, SMA200 at 0.5825) with recent session closes pushing below the 10-day closing low. Retail sentiment data retail positioning shows an extreme 87% long / 13% short bias, creating a strong contrarian signal against retail buyers who are attempting to bottom-fish. Fundamental backing remains weak as New Zealand's Economic Surprise Index sits at a strong negative reading of -26.7 (8 beats vs 13 misses), pointing to persistent macroeconomic underperformance. CFTC Leveraged Funds hold a net short of -22,722 contracts (long% 24.3%, 52-week percentile 25), reflecting institutional alignment with the broader downtrend. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/USD, contrarian fade against extreme retail long positioning. Catalyst: US Michigan Consumer Sentiment at 15:00 UTC. Risk: Unexpected RBNZ hawkish policy pivot that forces institutional short covering.
